messages.subject: Question about pc.prior
parts:
What is my default pc.prior? How to check this? 

According to INLA-workshop, the speaker lady said "it control the speed of variance go to zero".   If I use pc.prior(1,0.2) means the probability of sd larger than 1 is 0.2. How this control the speed? 

How should I balance these two parameters? I can say pr.prior(1000,0.0001), I can also say pr.prior(0.5, 0.5) which is more correct?

Thanks

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Question about pc.prior
parts:
the pc.prior has to be worked out in each case, but its basically and
exponential prior in distance between the model and its simplification
as suggested by that parameter.

please see the paper in Stat.Sci 2017 (I think) about it [which also
answer your second question].

for variance or precision, the pc.prior is usually exponential in the
std.deviation

Best
H
